'''''Dianella ensifolia''''' is a [[flowering plant]], of the family [[Asphodelaceae]]. It is native to southern China, India, Japan, Madagascar, [[Malesia]], [[the Pacific Islands]], Singapore, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, and tropical Asia. Its common names include umbrella [[Dracaena (plant)|dracaena]], common [[Dianella (plant)|dianella]], siak-siak, and [[flax lily]].<ref name="NParks">{{cite web |title=Dianella ensifolia (L.) DC. |url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/5/1/5194 |website=National Parks |publisher=Flora Fauna Web |access-date=30 March 2022}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Dianella ensifolia'' is a terrestrial plant that can grow in [[grassland]]s, or primary [[rainforest]]s in [[Tropical rainforest|tropical]] areas. The plant's [[Plant anatomy|anatomy]] consists of branching [[rhizome]]s, and flowering [[Plant stem|stems]], that can reach up to two meters. Its [[leaf]] blades are pointed and tapered at both ends. When flowering, it produces a [[Shoot (botany)|shoot]] about 60 cm (23.6 in) long. It has white petals, with orange/yellow [[Stamen|anthers.]] Once it is [[Pollination|pollinated]] by insects, it will produce [[Berry|berries]] that are dark blue/purple, and about 1.5 cm (0.59 in) wide. These berries contain 3-6 [[seed]]s, that are often eaten by native birds.<ref name="NParks" />

== Common names ==
Other common names for ''Dianella ensifolia'' include umbrella dracaena, common dianella, and [[flax lily]].<ref name="NParks" />

== Etymology ==
The [[Latin name]] ''Dianella'' is after [[Diana (mythology)|Diana]], a goddess in [[Greek mythology]]. Further, the Latin ''ensifolia'' is used to regard the sword-shaped leaves of the plant.<ref name="NParks" />

== Phytochemical properties and chemotaxonomic significance ==
A 2017 study investigated the roots of the ''Dianella ensifolia,'' and was able to isolate eleven compounds. When broken into groups, this would constitute two [[Aromatic compound|aromatics]], two [[chromone]]s, and 7 [[flavonoid]]s.<ref name="Tang">{{cite journal |last1=Tang |first1=Ben-qin |last2=Chen |first2=Zhen-yang |last3=Sun |first3=Jian-bo |last4=Lee |first4=Simon Ming-yuen |last5=Lu |first5=Jian-lin |title=Phytochemical and chemotaxonomic study on Dianella ensifolia (L.) DC |journal=Biochemical Systematics and Ecology |date=2010 |volume=17 |pages=12–14 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0305197817300467 |access-date=30 March 2022}}</ref>

The compounds found in ''D. ensifolia'' can be correlated with different [[Taxonomic rank|taxonomic levels]], including the [[species]], [[genus]], and [[Family (taxonomy)|family]]. The research concluded the structural skeletons of the compounds found in the ''D. ensifolia,'' are found within the species of ''Dianella,'' and Liliaceae. This would correlate the species to the genus. Further, the aromatics, chromones, and flavonoids were first isolated from the species itself of the genus, and thus, could serve as markers for the identification of ''Dianella ensifolia''.<ref name="Tang" />

== Chemical composition and medicinal use of essential oil ==
In 2020 [[essential oil]] of the ''D. ensifolia'' was chemically analyzed, and tested for its [[Antibiotic|antibacterial]], [[antioxidant]], and [[Cytotoxicity|cytotoxic]] properties. The main components of the plant essential oil were identified as allo-aromadendrene (7.3%), [[Geranylacetone]] (6.2%), Hexahydrofarnesyl acetone (4.4%), [[Longifolene]] (4.2%), and [[Caryophyllene|β-caryophyllene]] (4.0%).<ref name="He">{{cite journal |last1=He |first1=Zi-Qian |last2=Shen |first2=Xue-Yuan |last3=Cheng |first3=Xe-Yu |last4=Want |first4=Ruo-Lan |last5=Lai |first5=Peng-Xiang |last6=Xing |first6=Xiang |title=Chemical Composition, Antibacterial, Antioxidant and Cytotoxic Activities of the Essential Oil of Dianella ensifolia |journal=Records of Natural Products |date=2020 |volume=14 |issue=2 |pages=160–165 |doi=10.25135/rnp.150.19.07.1321 |s2cid=204892762 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

When examined individually, these compounds exhibit potent antimicrobial activity, [[Cytotoxicity|cytotoxic]] activity, the potential to inhibit cell growth and proliferation, and in-vivo protective effects against juglone-induced [[oxidative stress]] in [[Nematode|roundworm]].<ref name="He" />

The essential oil was investigated further for its antibacterial activity, and it was determined that it effectively inhibited the growth of numerous bacterial strains, including ''[[Bacillus subtilis]]'' ATCC 6633 and ''[[Staphylococcus aureus]]'' ATCC 6538. This effect was associated with the compounds geranylacetone, hexahydrofarnesyl acetone, longifolene, and β-caryophyllene, found in the essential oil.<ref name="He" />

The cytotoxicity of the essential oil was also examined against liver [[Hepatitis|hepatocellular]] cells, and human breast [[adenocarcinoma]] cell line. The essential oil of the ''D. ensifolia'' displayed a dose-dependent effect on both tumor cell lines. This may be contributed to the reported tumor motility inhibition, and tumor aggression inhibition of β-caryophyllene.<ref name="He" />

== Extract medicinal use ==
A study conducted in 2010 screened plant extracts for [[antioxidant]]s, and determined that the extract of ''Dianella ensifolia'' was both a strong antioxidant, and an agent that could be used to reduce skin [[hyperpigmentation]]. The extract of ''Dianella ensifolia'', 1-(2,4-dihydrophenyl)-3-(2,4- dimethoxy-3-methylphenyl) propane (DP), was found to inhibit a [[Radical (chemistry)|free radical]], which is linked to hyperpigmentation, and ultraviolet-C induced [[lipid oxidation]]. The extract from the plant was then tested against two pharmaceutical topical treatments. It was concluded that the plant extract, containing DP, had an increased rate of fading compared to the other treatments containing [[hydroquinone]].<ref name="Derm">{{cite journal |last1=Mammone |first1=Thomas |last2=Muizzuddin |first2=Neelam |last3=Declercq |first3=Lieve |last4=Clio |first4=Dominique |last5=Corstjens |first5=Hugo |last6=Sente |first6=Ilse |last7=Van Rillaer |first7=Katrin |last8=Matsui |first8=Mary |last9=Niki |first9=Yoko |last10=Ichihashi |first10=Masamitsu |last11=Paolo |first11=U. Giacomon |last12=Dan |first12=Yarosh |title=Modification of skin discoloration by a topical treatment containing an extract of Dianella ensifolia: a potent antioxidant |journal=Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology |date=2010 |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=89–95 |doi=10.1111/j.1473-2165.2010.00491.x |pmid=20618553 |s2cid=40900725 |url=http://explore.bl.uk/primo_library/libweb/action/display.do?tabs=detailsTab&gathStatTab=true&ct=display&fn=search&doc=ETOCRN272420323&indx=1&recIds=ETOCRN272420323 |access-date=30 March 2022|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
